title: Bits to a number
description:
Write `fromBinary(bits)`. It is given a string of `0` and `1` characters, most significant bit first, and returns the number those bits stand for.

`fromBinary("1010")` is 10. `fromBinary("01001101")` is 77. An empty string is 0.

Do the conversion yourself, using place values. The standard library's conversion functions and `std::bitset` are not allowed here.
hints: Think about how you read a decimal number one digit at a time: for 345 you could say "3", then "3 tens and 4, so 34", then "34 tens and 5, so 345". Each new digit multiplies what you have by ten and adds itself.
Binary is the same with two instead of ten. For each character: double the value so far, then add 1 if the character is `'1'`.
A range-based loop reads the characters in order: `for (char bit : bits)`. Compare with the character `'1'`, in single quotes, not the number 1.
rules: Work the value out yourself with place values, without a library conversion.
